title: the panel tells the truth about its own state
description: Tasks: (1) Overview branches on manifestExists && !rollup and shows the existing findings box instead of 'No plan yet'. (2) A failed poll shows a persistent offline banner and disables Save; a failed save says nothing was written. (3) Save writes only changed keys, so a default list is not frozen into the config. (4) The example's .claude/state is ignored. (5) GET / requires the token the URL already carries, the pidfile is 0600, and SECURITY.md says the panel trusts every local process of the same user. (6) The Azure DevOps card and column appear only when meta.ado is configured.
desiredOutcome: the panel shows an unreadable manifest as unreadable, shows a stopped server as stopped with Save disabled, saves only the keys a user changed, leaves a clean tree in the example, and serves its token only to a request that already carries it

findings.issue: The config patch is diffed against the wrong base: the draft is cloned from STATE.config when the form renders, but Save computes configPatch(STATE.config, cfg) against whatever STATE.config holds at Save time, and the disk refresh replaces STATE wholesale even while the form is dirty (it only skips the re-render). A user edits key a, another writer changes key b, the poll refreshes, and Save sends b back at its old value - reverting the other writer's change, while the confirm dialog lists b as the user's change.
findings.resolution: Snapshot the base when the form renders and diff every config editor's draft against its own base (configChanges, the edit tracker, discard rows and configPatch), resetting the base from the server's result after a save; a vitest case renders, dirties a, swaps STATE.config with b changed, saves, and asserts the patch names only a.

findings.issue: Now that GET / needs the token, the URL commands/panel.md tells the agent to relay from --status (printed with ?t=<hidden>) and any bare or bookmarked panel address answer a raw JSON 403 that says nothing about where the real URL is; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] has no entry for the change.
findings.resolution: Answer a tokenless GET / with a plain-text 403 that names the way back (/audit:panel status, the pidfile, or relaunch) without echoing a token; say in panel.md that the printed URL is redacted and will not open the page; add an [Unreleased] entry.

findings.issue: The pidfile's temp (.claude/audit-panel.json.tmp-<hex>) holds the live token but is not in _PANEL_PRIVATE_FILES and is never swept, so a launch killed between open and replace leaves a token-bearing untracked file; the docstring's owner-only-from-the-instant claim is POSIX-only; a pidfile written 0644 by a pre-upgrade server keeps that mode until stop or relaunch.
findings.resolution: Ignore and sweep stale audit-panel.json.tmp-* files, limit the docstring claim to POSIX, and tighten an existing pidfile on status or the already-running branch.

findings.issue: adoVisible counts linked tasks and phases but not linked bugs, so a plan whose only ADO record is a bug link gets the collapsed 'not set up for this plan' card and its banner is hidden.
findings.resolution: Count linked.bugs too, with a vitest row holding only a bug link.

findings.issue: The guide still says the token is required on every /api/* call (leaving out /) and says nothing of the owner-only pidfile; the panel parts README still describes run-status.js as the poll and its badges, though it now owns the liveness state confirmSave reads, and does not name overview.js's planState as a cross-view helper.
findings.resolution: Extend the guide sentence to / and the owner-only pidfile; update the two README rows.

findings.issue: SECURITY.md's panel trust-boundary account is now incomplete: it does not say the page itself is token-guarded, that the token rests in .claude/audit-panel.json written owner-only (POSIX), or that a pre-upgrade server keeps the old exposure until restarted. SECURITY.md is owned by another phase.
findings.resolution: Reconcile in the phase that owns SECURITY.md when the branches meet: add a short panel trust-boundary paragraph covering the three points.

tasks.title: Show a stopped panel server as offline and refuse writes while it is
tasks.description: When the server stops with a tab open, the page keeps looking live, Save still opens its dialog, and the PUT rejects into an uncaught TypeError with nothing on screen. The poll owns liveness. The first failed poll paints a persistent page-level offline banner, placed like the build-stale notice and wearing .findings warn, sharing that notice's placement rule in app-shell.css rather than adding a second. It also disables every write control, reached through data- attributes, and the next poll that answers clears both. In api(), a write whose fetch rejects resolves to a refusal-shaped answer, so every save path renders it through findingsBox and saveOutcome. Its words state what the page knows: the server did not answer, no write is confirmed, and the edits are still in the form. That is the honest form of 'nothing was written', because a rejected fetch cannot tell a refused connection from an answer lost after the write. Print the pins with `python3 tools/count-ui-pins.py` first; besides the gates listed, run `npx vitest run`.

add: tools/ui-tests/server-offline.test.mjs: a PUT whose fetch rejects resolves to ok false with a finding saying the server did not answer and the edits are still in the form, while a GET whose fetch rejects still rejects
tools/ui-tests/server-offline.test.mjs: a poll whose fetch rejects marks the page offline and the next poll that answers clears it; an answer that arrives with ok false never marks it offline
tools/ui-tests/server-offline.test.mjs: while offline, confirmSave refuses with the offline sentence and opens no dialog
plugins/audit/tests/test__panel_page.py: the existing failed-poll pin is restated so the poll's catch sets the offline state instead of swallowing the failure

outcome.technical: core.js api(): a write whose fetch rejects resolves to a refusal-shaped answer carrying a no-answer finding; a read whose fetch rejects still rejects, tagged no-answer. run-status.js: the poll owns liveness - a rejected poll sets an offline state that marks the root, adds one page-level notice and makes write controls (reached through data- hooks) unavailable, and the next poll that answers clears both, handing back only what it took. write-confirmation.js: confirmSave refuses while offline before any dialog; saveOutcome renders the no-answer case. app-shell.css shares one placement rule between the offline notice and the build-stale notice. The D9 pin is restated; a vitest suite covers the behaviour with allow twins. The panel screenshots were re-captured because the panel sources moved. Left for later: the report button has only an id and is not on the control list, and appearance-view.js chains a read after its theme writes.
outcome.descriptive: When the panel server stops with a tab open, the page now shows that it is offline, marks its write controls unavailable and refuses Save, and a write that gets no answer says the server did not answer and the edits are still in the form, instead of failing silently.

intentCheck.basis: audit-reviewer (task mode): every write path receives the refusal answer; one shared placement rule; no findings; pre-existing appearance-view.js gap recorded

tasks.title: Save only the config keys the form changed
tasks.description: Settings Save sends the whole config the form holds, so the server rewrites keys nobody changed. Adding one entry to a list key that was unset (exemptGlobs) writes the whole shipped default list into the file without saying so. Send a patch instead: one entry per changed key, addressed by key segments rather than a dotted string, because a pricing key can contain a dot. Apply it in _panel_write through write_config(mutate=...) against the config read under the write lock; COMPATIBILITY.md puts the panel's HTTP endpoints outside the version contract, so the payload may change shape. The confirm dialog marks a list row whose key was unset and has a shipped default as pinning that default, so later plugin defaults stop reaching the project. Its note also says the file is rewritten in canonical JSON layout, because the stdlib keeps no formatting. Besides the gates listed, run `npx vitest run`.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__panel_write.py: a config patch changing one key writes that key and leaves every other key's value as read from disk, a float such as 5.0 included
plugins/audit/tests/test__panel_write.py: the patch is applied to the config read under the write lock, so a change another writer made to a different key after the form loaded survives
plugins/audit/tests/test__panel_write.py: a patch addresses keys by segment, so a pricing key containing a dot is written as one key

tools/ui-tests/config-patch.test.mjs: the patch built from the form carries only the changed paths, a removal for a key set back to its default, and a pin flag on a list key set from absent where a shipped default exists

outcome.technical: Settings Save sends a patch instead of the whole config. _panel_write gains apply_config_patch and write_config_patch: each entry addresses a key by a list of segments (a dotted string is refused, because a pricing key can hold a dot) and either sets a value or removes the key; every entry is validated before any read or lock; the patch is applied through write_config(mutate=...) to the config read under the write lock, so keys nobody changed keep the values read from disk and another writer's change to a different key survives; removals run before writes and delete containers they empty; write_config's own validation still runs on the result. panel-server routes PUT /api/config to it. In the page, cfDiff decides by presence: a key absent from the draft is a removal and a key present is written even when it equals the shipped default, so an explicit value stays pinned as COMPATIBILITY.md promises; the list editor no longer writes a drawn-in default into the draft until an entry actually changes. The confirm dialog marks a row that pins a non-empty shipped default list, and its note says the file is rewritten in canonical JSON layout. Python cases cp1-cp5 and a vitest file that includes a case sending the page's patch through Python's apply_config_patch; the pin note's placement is checked by rendering the dialog.
outcome.descriptive: Saving Settings in the panel now writes only the keys the user changed, on top of the file as it is on disk, and a value set equal to today's default stays written as an explicit choice.

intentCheck.basis: audit-reviewer (task mode, opus): matches; three findings fixed as proposed (presence decides removal, pin only for a non-empty default, dialog placement case), each guarded by a mutation

tasks.title: Make the panel's state directory ignore itself
tasks.description: The first panel launch writes .claude/state/panel-openstate.json through a plain makedirs. In a project where no hook has run yet, the committed acme-store example included, the state directory then has no ignore rule and the launch leaves an untracked file, contrary to examples/README.md. Have _panel_runstate.record_opened create the directory through the hooks' own _config.ensure_local_dir (reached via _paths.hooks_config()), which drops the same self-ignoring .gitignore every other plugin-local directory gets, instead of adding an ignore line for the example only. Correct the first-launch sentence in examples/README.md. In the plugin README, name the state file beside the pidfile and the launch log, naming the files rather than counting them.

outcome.technical: _panel_runstate.record_opened creates the state directory through the hooks' ensure_local_dir (reached via _paths.hooks_config()), which drops a self-ignoring .gitignore on first creation and never overwrites an existing one. tasks.title: Require the session token on GET / and write the pidfile 0600
tasks.description: GET / hands the page, with the session token substituted into it, to any local request that passes the Host check. The pidfile holding the same token is written with whatever mode the umask gives. Route / through the token guard the API already uses. The printed URL and the pidfile's url already carry ?t=, and a relaunch opens that url, so the browser and the screenshot tool keep working. Write the pidfile owner-only, tighten an existing one, and update the safety line in commands/panel.md to say the page itself needs the token. This phase's description also names a SECURITY.md sentence on the panel's trust boundary; that file belongs to the phase that owns SECURITY.md and is not edited here.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_panel_server.py: GET / without the token answers 403 and its body carries no token, while GET /?t=<token> answers 200 with the page

plugins/audit/tests/test_panel_server.py: the pidfile is written owner read/write only (0600), also when a 0644 file was already there; skipped by name, with the mechanism, on a platform without POSIX modes
plugins/audit/tests/test_panel_server.py: /favicon.ico still answers without the token

outcome.technical: panel-server.py's GET / now goes through the same guard every /api/* route uses (host check and token), so the page, which carries the session token, is no longer handed to any local request that passes the Host check; /favicon.ico still answers without a token. The printed URL and the pidfile's url already carry ?t=, so the browser, a relaunch and the screenshot tool keep working (tools/capture-screenshots.mjs navigates to the pidfile's url). The pidfile is written owner-only from the start: a temp file in the same directory opened with O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL at 0o600, a defensive fchmod on the descriptor where available (a failure is reported on stderr, not swallowed), then os.replace onto the real path, so there is no create-then-chmod window and an existing wider file is replaced; a failed write removes its temp file. commands/panel.md's safety line says the page itself needs the token, and CONTRIBUTING.md's module-graph passage no longer says / hands the token to any loopback client, keeping the old measurement as history. Cases in test_panel_server.py: GET / without the token is 403 with the token absent from the body, with it 200; /favicon.ico needs none; a fresh pidfile is 0600, an existing 0644 one is tightened, and under umask 0o022 with os.chmod made a no-op the pidfile is still 0600 with no temp file left. SECURITY.md's panel trust-boundary sentence belongs to the phase that owns SECURITY.md and is not edited here.
outcome.descriptive: The panel's page now asks for the same per-launch token as its API, so another local process can no longer read the token off the page, and the file that stores it is private to the user from the moment it is written.

intentCheck.basis: audit-reviewer (task mode), two rounds: matches; the medium finding (a create-then-chmod window on the pidfile) fixed with an O_EXCL owner-only temp and replace, proven under a no-op chmod; the low (a stale CONTRIBUTING sentence) fixed
